generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: DYNA-2 PROVES SCALING LAWS FOR ROBOTICS: 1 MILLION HOURS OF HUMAN VIDEO UNLOCKS ZERO-SHOT DEXTERITY
Summary: Dyna-2 is a world-action model (WAM) pre-trained on over one million hours of human video data. Its existence proves that scaling human video data predictably improves zero-shot performance on unseen robot hardware. Dyna-2 achieved an 87% pass rate in real-world zero-shot deployments at customer sites, vastly outperforming the 46% pass rate of its VLA predecessor, Dyna-1. The model uses a new one-step video generation distillation pipeline that drops inference latency by two orders of magnitude for downstream planning.

Editorial idea:
Human video data is becoming a training ground for machines that must act in unfamiliar physical situations.

Central subject:
A robot learning dexterous movement from a vast archive of human actions

Visual relationship:
The system transfers patterns from observed human behavior to unfamiliar hardware, turning recorded experience into reliable real-world action.

Composition:
Show a sequence of human hand movements fading into a different mechanical gripper performing the same task, with the final action visibly succeeding in an unfamiliar setting. Keep the transformation continuous rather than presenting separate objects.

Permitted literal elements:
human hands demonstrating a dexterous task
a mechanical gripper repeating the movement
a varied physical workspace suggesting unseen hardware
subtle indication of repeated video frames or motion capture without rendered text

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
racks
chips
laptops
robots as generic humanoid figures
clouds
shields
arrows
charts
skyscrapers
chess
handshakes
split-screen conflict
logos
rendered text
unsupported laboratory details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Do not depict the robot as generally intelligent or humanlike.
Do not imply that the model solved every task or operates without human-derived training.
Do not use generic futuristic automation imagery disconnected from zero-shot dexterity.
Do not add performance figures visually unless they are represented without text and factually tiedも

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
